subject.name: Duplicate posting on client retry
subject.summary: A retried POST /v1/transfers created a second transfer when Redis was unavailable
subject.description: Duplicate transfers / double postings after a client retry: the X-Idempotency-Key check lived only in Redis and failed open during the Redis failover, so the retry after a 502 posted twice. Symptoms: duplicate transfer, double charge, balance off by the transfer amount, ledger_idempotency_conflicts_total flat while duplicates appear. Synonyms: double posting, duplicate transfer, idempotency failed open, redis failover duplicates.

properties.symptom_signature: duplicate transfer after 502 retry; idempotency key miss during redis outage

operations.description: Seen in INC-12 (2026-08-30) after a Redis failover: clients retried POST /v1/transfers after a 502 and the idempotency key lookup failed open.

subject.name: Retry-After header on 502
subject.summary: Added Retry-After header; did not stop duplicates
subject.description: Failed attempt: sending Retry-After on 502 responses so clients back off. Duplicates persisted because the idempotency check itself was the gap.

operations.description: First attempt added Retry-After: 2 on 502s; clients still retried and duplicates continued during the outage.

subject.name: Postgres fallback for idempotency keys
subject.summary: Check X-Idempotency-Key in Postgres idempotency_keys when Redis is down; fail closed with 503 if both are unavailable
subject.description: Fix for duplicate postings on retry: transfers.py now consults the Postgres idempotency_keys table when the Redis lookup errors, and returns 503 instead of posting when neither store answers. Files: src/ledgerly/api/transfers.py, migrations/0042_idempotency_keys.py. Verified against the INC-12 replay. Synonyms: idempotency fallback, fail closed, redis outage fix.

properties.fix_steps: consult idempotency_keys table on Redis error; 503 when both stores fail

operations.description: PR #212: check the idempotency key in the Postgres idempotency_keys table when Redis is unavailable; verified by replaying INC-12 traffic in staging.

subject.name: PR #212 verification run
subject.summary: Replay of INC-12 traffic in staging produced no duplicates

operations.description: CI replay of INC-12 traffic: 0 duplicates across 12k retried transfers

subject.name: Plaid sync cursor reset after re-auth
subject.summary: Reconciler re-imported 30 days of bank transactions after an item re-auth reset the sync cursor
subject.description: Balance drift / duplicate bank transactions after a Plaid item re-authentication: ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED, the update-mode Link flow, and the reconciler starting transactions/sync with cursor=null so every historical transaction came back as added. Symptoms: balance drift, duplicate bank entries, recon report shows thousands of unmatched rows. Synonyms: cursor reset, plaid re-auth duplicates, transactions/sync from scratch, ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED.

properties.symptom_signature: ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED then reconciler imports 30 days again; balance drift

operations.description: After an item re-auth (ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED) the reconciler restarted transactions/sync from a null cursor and re-imported 30 days of transactions.

subject.name: Persist Plaid sync cursor per item
subject.summary: Store transactions/sync cursor on plaid_items and dedupe by transaction_id
subject.description: Fix for the cursor reset: plaid_feed.py stores next_cursor on plaid_items after every page and the importer upserts by Plaid transaction_id, so a re-auth or restart never re-imports history. Files: src/ledgerly/sync/plaid_feed.py, migrations/0044_plaid_cursor.py. Synonyms: cursor persistence, transaction_id dedupe.

properties.fix_steps: persist next_cursor per item; upsert by transaction_id

operations.description: PR #231: persist the sync cursor per plaid_item and dedupe imported rows by transaction_id; a re-auth keeps the cursor.
